pr_title: fix(rust, python) respect time zone in date_range
pr_comments: Awesome! Can you undraft. Can include it in today's release. :)
sure, undrafting for now - currently it's parsing the time zone each time, did you want to take it like this and leave perf improvements to a follow-up?
Oh, right. Let's optimize directly. Can release without the patch. 👍

Cool, have updated, it now parses the time zone once in `date_range_impl` and then just passes it down

For parts which don't (yet) respect the time zone properly (groupby_dynamic), I'm just passing `None` such as to not change the current behaviour. But what's introduced in this PR would make it easier to properly address groupby_dynamic and resample later

Passing `None` when a function expects `Option<&impl TimeZoneTrait>` errors, so I passed `None::<chrono::FixedOffset>` as `chrono` is typically already available in most places (I did have to add it to `polars-lazy/polars-plan` under the `date-offset` feature though)

issue_context.title: Ambiguous time bug
issue_context.body:
### Polars version checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Issue description

In some functions in `polars` certain times with different timezone are considered `ambiguous` (e.g `2021-11-07T01:00:00CDT` and  `2021-11-07T01:00:00CST`) whereas they are not as the timezone is well specified. This happens in the following example but also in `groupby`.
I'm not sure why in some other function they are not considered `amiguous` though, e.g in `convert_time_zone` works fine.

``` python
>>> pl.date_range(datetime(2021,11,7), datetime(2021,11,8), "1h", time_zone="US/Central")
thread '<unnamed>' panicked at 'Ambiguous local time, ranging from 2021-11-07T01:00:00CDT to 2021-11-07T01:00:00CST', /Users/runner/.cargo/registry/src/github.com-1ecc6299db9ec823/chrono-0.4.23/src/offset/mod.rs:189:17
Traceback (most recent call last):

>>> pl.date_range(datetime(2021,11,7), datetime(2021,11,8), "1h", time_zone="UTC").dt.convert_time_zone("US/Central")
shape: (25,)
```

```python
>>> df = pl.DataFrame({"time":t2, "value": range(1441)})
```

Sorry for the `timezone` pounding ... 

### Reproducible example

```python
from datetime import datetime
import polars as pl
t1 = pl.date_range(datetime(2021,11,7), datetime(2021,11,8), "1h", time_zone="US/Central")  # fails
t2 = pl.date_range(datetime(2021,11,7), datetime(2021,11,8), "1h", time_zone="UTC").dt.convert_time_zone("US/Central") # works as intended

t2 =pl.date_range(datetime(2021,11,7), datetime(2021,11,8), "1m", time_zone="UTC").dt.convert_time_zone("US/Central")
df = pl.DataFrame({"time":t2, "value": range(1441)})
df.groupby_dynamic("time", every="1h").agg(pl.col("value").mean())
```


### Expected behavior

I expect `t1` in the example to works as `t2`.

`2021-11-07T01:00:00CDT` and  `2021-11-07T01:00:00CST` are not ambiguous as they are different times (based on the timezone).

review_comments: Do we already have an issue for this? That means we validate timezone upon entry in the API right? I like that idea as it removes a lot of assertions downstream.

There's https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/7434

The time zone itself is validated upon entry (e.g. here it's validated in the entry to `date_range_impl`) - the reason for the unwrap isn't that the time zone might not be valid, but that adding a non-fixed offset might result in an ambiguous or non-existent date

For example, if you were to start on `'2021-10-07T01:00 US/Central'` and to add a month, you would end up on `'2021-11-07T01:00 US/Central'` - problem is, is that `'2021-11-07T01:00 CDT'` or `'2021-11-07T01:00 CST'`? Until https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/6672 is addressed, I think the only option would be to error
